recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and avoid adding redundant prose for FHIR-5999. Any further work should proceed under later, issue-specific resource-definition or rendering/tooling tickets such as FHIR-54847 or the IG Publisher issue referenced by FHIR-44344.
issue_request: FHIR-5999 was a Published FHIR-core profiles change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for a spreadsheet/tooling way to place different bindings on the different datatypes of a choice ([x]) element. The final resolution said slicing by type for non-repeating elements was supported by the tools and the original problem was no longer an issue.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-5999. The apparent historical application is legacy commit 320e08d887d55dafdb49caef913bc62bfc1e22bf, which clarified that slicing can be used on elements that do not repeat but have a choice of datatypes and updated ElementDefinition.slicing to allow slicing for resources with a choice of types.
additional_context: FHIR-28619 later rejected general slicing of arbitrary non-repeating elements while confirming the intended boundary: non-repeating slicing is presently supported only by type for polymorphic elements. Later FHIR-54847 and a 2026 Zulip discussion expose a separate core resource-definition/spreadsheet limitation, and FHIR-44344 concerns extension rendering/tooling; neither changes the profile-focused conclusion for FHIR-5999.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/terminologies.html instructs authors to slice a choice element by type when a binding applies only to a specific type; source/profiling.html documents type discriminators for polymorphic elements and gives Observation.value[x] with vocabulary bindings as an example; source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml permits slicing for choice types; and active Observation profile source demonstrates a type slice with a required binding.

related_jiras.note: Later FHIR-I no-change decision confirms that non-repeating slicing is limited to polymorphic type slicing, matching the current interpretation of FHIR-5999.
Later OO ServiceRequest binding work exposes a separate core resource-definition/tooling issue and is not a duplicate of the profile-focused FHIR-5999 request.
FHIR Extension Pack rendering/tooling concern about choice bindings is outside the core source decision for FHIR-5999.
